steps.text: Heat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Place butter in the bottom of a 9x13 baking dish and bring it to the preheated oven.
Mix together Bisquick, paprika, salt and pepper in a bowl; add chicken and move it coat all sides. Transfer chicken pieces, skin sides down, into hot buttered baking dish.

Bake 35 minutes in preheated oven; turn chicken skin side up and bake about 15 minutes longer or until juices run clear. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part, without touching the bone, should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Oven-Baked Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Why deep-fry? Bake juicy, tender chicken with a tasty seasoned coating. It’s the start of a great meal.
raw_recipe.name: Oven-Baked Chicken

review.reviewBody: Great taste, but took off a star since the Bisquick mixture had a hard time sticking to the chicken. Next time I think I'd first dip the chicken in a mix of egg and milk.

My family loved it! I dipped the chicken in a egg & milk mixture prior to dipping in flour mix (I did add a little Dash to flour mixture). I bought a pack of thighs instead of a whole chicken ....the meat stays really moist and fits in pan equally. I lined my pan with tin foil....easy & quick clean up!

I made this tonight for Wednesday Chicken Dinner night. It was delicious and juicy. The only thing that I changed was that I soaked my chicken in buttermilk for eight hours, rinsed and patted it dry before breading it. My husband always loved his grandma's oven fried chicken but I could never duplicate it, until now! I think the key is to put the chicken in the preheated pan with the melted butter. I had chicken legs because that's what was on sale. Eight chicken legs for $1.79 was quite a deal! I'll be doing this again and again, with my husband's encouragement!

I didn't have Bisquick on hand so used pancake mix instead. For added flavor, I added Lawry's seasoned salt to the dry ingredients. Sprayed butter cooking spray on the chicken before coating. The temperature and time given cooked the chicken to perfection. Delicious chicken using a very simple and easy recipe. Will definitely make again.

I used 2 large breasts (about 1.3 lbs total) and put it in a 9x9 pan. I used all the same amounts, but I also added a 1/4 tsp of garlic powder and chopped up 1 tbsp of fresh Italian herbs from my garden. Be careful because it cooks much faster. I did 30 minutes at 400 degrees flipping them after 20 minutes. Next time I'll shave 3 or 4 minutes off. My wife loved it!

I made it and dipped the pieces in a egg wash per a recommendation. I used Pioneer Buttermilk Pancake and Biscuit Mix. I have cornflakes but I didn’t want to change the recipe and wish the was a thumbs down option for comments from the peanut gallery.
this was delicious. my changes were: adding garlic powder to the store brand Bisquick, baking in cast iron, added a little bit of peanut oil to the butter on the bottom and it did not stick it all.

I first made this chicken over 50 years ago. I lined the pan with foil, for easy clean up. I used shortening rather than butter and melted it in the foil lined pan while I prepped the bisquick mixture. I put the bisquick along with seasonings in a large sandwich bag (whatever it was back then) and threw in a piece of chicken and shook it to cover the chicken - my version of "shake-n-bake."

I have tried several baked chicken recipes and this one is the best one by far!! My husband LOVED it. The only thing I did different was I used skinless boneless chicken thighs and cut down the times to 30 mins, then turned them, then another 10 mins. They were perfectly crispy and juicy. Delicious!!

So good! Great cooking directions. The hot temperature gives a nice crust and juicy inside. I used Rosemary "LiveGFree" gluten free crackers and some season salt to make it gluten free. Dipped chicken in egg then cracker which I turned to crumbs in food processor.

This chicken dish was flavorful and the coating was crispy and delicious!!!! I read that one person said he/she had trouble with the Bisquick mixture sticking. I blended all the dry ingredients in a large plastic bag and put two pieces of chicken at a time into the bag and shook the bag until the pieces were well coated. I had no problem using this method with the coating not sticking! Each piece was evenly coated as well!
This was so easy and delicious! I did a light egg/milk dip first and added garlic and onion powders. Going in our favorites file!
No it was great just the way it was
I’ve been making this for years and the chicken always comes out perfectly! It’s a family (and chef 😉) favorite for sure!
